passage:
A company built a vertical farm inside an old warehouse. Vegetables grew on shelves under special lights.
Students visited and saw lettuce growing without soil. Water and nutrients moved through pipes. Computers controlled temperature and light.
The manager said vertical farms can grow food near cities and use less land. But they also need electricity and careful management.
Students debated whether such farms could replace traditional farms. Most decided they were not a replacement, but another tool.
The visit showed that future food may come from many systems. Fields, greenhouses, rooftops, and warehouses may all become part of feeding cities.
